text: TSA estimates the hour burden associated with the initial submission of security programs to be 4 hours for each of the 350 average annual new entrants of aircraft operators, foreign air carriers, and IACs for an average annual hour burden of 1,400 hours.  TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage rate of $94.63 for Security Coordinators to estimate the total annual hour cost burden of the new security program process.  The total annual hour burden cost due to the application process is estimated to be $132,477.  Table 1, at the end of this response, summarizes these calculations.

text: TSA estimates the hour burden associated with the security program renewals via IACMS to be 4 hours for each of the 3,700 IACs for an average annual hour burden of 14,800 hours. TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage of $94.63 for Security Coordinators to estimate the total annual hour cost burden of the new security program process.  The total annual hour burden cost due to the application process is estimated to be $1,400,470.  TSA estimates 37 IACs will file an appeal of rejected or incomplete renewals at 5 hours per appeal for an average annual hour burden of 185 hours.  TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage of $94.63 for Security Coordinators to estimate the total annual hour cost burden of the new security program process.  The total annual hour burden cost due to the application process is estimated to be $17,506.  Table 1, at the end of this response, summarizes these calculations.

text: TSA also issues amendments to its security programs.  These amendments are either TSA-initiated or industry requested.  There are approximately 600 TSA-issued amendments per year.  TSA estimates a 1 hour burden to comply with a TSA issued amendment, for an annual hour burden of 600 hours.  Industry requested amendments typically are asking for approval from TSA for existing business practices, and TSA estimates a 1 hour burden for the 946 average annual industry requested amendments, for an annual hour burden of 946 hours.  TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage of $94.63 for Security Coordinators to estimate the total annual hour cost burden of the new security program process.  The total annual hour burden cost due to the application process is estimated to be $56,776.  Table 1, at the end of this response, summarizes these calculations.

text: For the KSMS, given that the IAC or aircraft operator must input a name, address, and telephone number, TSA estimates it will take 2 minutes for the 476,167 electronic submissions for a total annual burden of 15,872 hours.  TSA uses a weighted average hourly loaded wage of $30.67 of IAC workers to estimate the total annual hour burden cost of the application process.  TSA estimates a total annual hour cost burden of $486,825 for electronic KSMS submissions.  Also for KSMS, TSA estimates it will take one hour for the 8,000 manual submissions for a total annual burden of 8,000 hours.  TSA uses a weighted average hourly loaded wage of $30.67 of IAC workers to estimate the total annual hour burden cost of the application process.  TSA estimates an annual hour cost burden of $245,372 for KSMS manual submissions.  Table 1, at the end of this response, summarizes these calculations.

text: TSA Principal Security Inspectors review updates and new submissions to the IACSSP.  TSA estimates this review takes 2 hours and 15 minutes (2.25 hours) per IAC.  Each of the 4,050 IACs must renew annually.  The total hour burden for the Federal Government for this task is 9,113.  The cost burden is based on the average loaded hourly wage rate for an SV I/J band TSA employee, which is $72.72 per hour.  The estimated cost to TSA to review the updates required of IACSSP and new submissions is $662,634 annually.  Table 3, below, summarizes this calculation.
